text:
acme_ben: Hey @maria_cs — after yesterday's model rollout our retrieval+rerank results are noticeably worse. We're seeing poor grounding and wrong citations for invoice/finance queries. MRR on our evaluation suite dropped from ~0.72 -> 0.46. Can you help?

maria_cs: Ugh, that's bad. Thanks for flagging. Do you have a short repro (query + expected top doc id vs actual)? Which API / model versions are you calling?

acme_ben: Yes — simple repro below. We hit the normal retrieval endpoint and then call the reranker. Before rollout the top-3 included doc ids [d:inv-8847, d:inv-8833, d:policy-22]. After rollout the top-3 are [d:blog-214, d:inv-8833, d:faq-9]. The top result is now a generic blog post, no invoice.

Request snippets:
```http
POST /v1/retrieval/query
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "model": "rr-encoder-1.5",
  "query": "order 8847 invoice total",
  "top_k": 50
}
```

```http
POST /v1/rerank
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "model": "reranker-v2",
  "query_id": "q-20270601-01",
  "candidate_ids": ["d:inv-8847","d:inv-8833","d:policy-22","d:blog-214","d:faq-9"],
  "top_k": 10
}
```

acme_ben: Expected top_k=1 => d:inv-8847, Actual => d:blog-214. We also have a small CSV with ~2k eval queries; overall recall @10 went from 0.88 -> 0.59. I can upload the CSV or share via secure link.

carlos_support: Thanks Ben — please share the CSV link. Also send the exact timestamps of your requests and the request ids (x-request-id header) so we can correlate logs.

acme_ben: Uploaded to the secure bucket: gs://acme-support/bugs/rerank-regression-20270601.csv. Example x-request-id: req-7a9f2e1b (seen around 1781203000).

maria_cs: @raj_ml and @sofia_eng can you take a look? We suspect the recent reranker-v2 rollout changed scoring weights. Customer is high priority — financial docs break customer workflows.

raj_ml: I'm on it. Quick check — deploy bot shows reranker-v2 rollout completed yesterday:

deploy-bot: reranker-v2 rollout: canary start 1781189500, canary -> 100% at 1781193600, pipeline-id=deploy-rr-20270601

raj_ml: Preliminary hypothesis: reranker-v2 fine-tune introduced stronger topical-similarity priors that favor blog/FAQ style documents for short queries. That can hurt precision for structured invoice queries which rely on numeric/entity matching. Need to run our eval harness against the customer's eval CSV and compare score distributions.

sofia_eng: If that's true we should offer an immediate mitigation: pin their workspace to reranker-v1 (the previous variant) or enable reranker-v2 with adjusted rerank_threshold/precision_bias for that customer. Which is faster?

raj_ml: Pinning to reranker-v1 for this customer is fastest (no code change on their side). We'll need to create a per-customer routing override in the control plane and roll that config. I can prepare the change and request a rapid rollout.

maria_cs: Please also attach diffs between reranker-v1 and v2 training data / objective. We need a quick customer-facing explanation.

raj_ml: Will do. I'll run the eval now and post results. Early sanity check: ran a small batch locally against the CSV head — MRR drop replicated (0.74 -> 0.47). Attaching a minimal example:

Before (reranker-v1):
1) d:inv-8847 (score 12.3)
2) d:inv-8833 (score 11.8)
3) d:policy-22 (score 9.2)

After (reranker-v2):
1) d:blog-214 (score 10.6)
2) d:inv-8833 (score 10.1)
3) d:faq-9 (score 9.9)

sofia_eng: Ok. Action plan: 1) Offer rollback (or customer pin) to affected accounts. 2) Run controlled A/B to measure long-tail degradation. 3) Adjust training weighting and push patch. 4) Put a hold on additional canaries for reranker-v2 until root cause confirmed.

maria_cs: Carlos, offer Acme a pin to reranker-v1 and a credit while we investigate. Make it low friction. I'll draft a customer note.

carlos_support: On it. Message ready: "We're sorry — we've identified a regression after a model rollout and can pin your workspace to the previous reranker variant (no code changes). We'll follow up with a timeline for a fix and a credit for impacted queries." Sending now. :pray:

acme_ben: Thanks, would appreciate the pin asap. Our compliance team needs citations to be stable.

raj_ml: I've created a control-plane override: route acme_corp -> reranker-v1, change-id cfg-pin-1781207. Requesting rollout now.

deploy-bot: config-change cfg-pin-1781207 applied to acme_corp at 1781207445, status=success

maria_cs: Confirmed? Ben, can you validate by re-running the repro?

acme_ben: Re-ran the same query — top result reverted to d:inv-8847. Verified. MRR head sample looks back to expected range. Thanks.

maria_cs: Great. Next steps for internal: raj_ml to produce a postmortem draft with root cause (training objective change -> recall drop) and mitigation (adjust training/data weighting). Engineering to gate further reranker rollouts with the retrieval/regression suite and require a "recall delta" SLO. Carlos to finalize customer communications and credit.

sofia_eng: I'll add a regression test to the deployment checklist: run the global retrieval/regression suite and fail rollout if recall@10 drops > 5% on any high-sensitivity testset.

raj_ml: I'll attach training diffs and evaluation artifacts by EOD.

carlos_support: Closing loop with customer in 24h. Assigning follow-ups in CRM.

acme_ben: Appreciate the quick turn. Please keep me posted on the permanent fix.

maria_cs: Thanks everyone. We'll treat as Sev-2 until root cause is addressed.
